faq.lastUpdated: Last checked against the app on July 30, 2026
faq.title: Questions and straight answers
faq.intro: Everything below describes what Scrlpets does today, not what it is going to do. Where a thing is not built yet, this page says so.

what.a: A place to follow animals and the people who raise and keep them, and to browse animals offered for sale or adoption. It is built for every species kept as a pet — dogs, cats, rabbits, birds, reptiles, fish and more — and the app uses each family's own vocabulary instead of forcing one animal's words onto another.

account.a: Not to look. Public profiles, animals, posts, listings and guides are readable without signing in. You need an account to publish anything, to send a message, or to ask a seller about a listing.

buy.q: Can I buy an animal on Scrlpets right now?
buy.a: No. Scrlpets does not process payments, and every money path is switched off in the database rather than merely hidden in the interface. You can ask a seller about a listing, and the conversation keeps that listing's details attached — but anything you agree after that happens between the two of you, off Scrlpets.

identity.a: Not yet. Identity checks are built to run through Stripe Identity and are not switched on. When they are, Stripe holds the documents and Scrlpets stores only whether the check passed. Until then, treat every account as unverified.

badge.q: What does a reviewed credential mean?
badge.a: Someone can submit a kennel licence, business registration, rescue or shelter registration, USDA licence, or breed club membership as a number and an issuing authority. No documents are uploaded. A person checks it against public records and approves or rejects it. That means a credential checked out — it does not mean Scrlpets visited anyone, inspected a facility, or met an animal.

health.a: No. Scrlpets does not examine, test or health-check any animal, and does not employ a vet. Health entries and reminders in the app are recorded by the animal's own keeper. They are that person's records, not a Scrlpets verification of anything.

rules.q: Someone is behaving badly. What can I do?
rules.a: Report the post, comment, listing or profile. Reports go to a queue a person works through, and they can dismiss the report, hide the content, or suspend the account. You can also block someone: a block hides them from your feed and your messages and severs follows in both directions. Their profile page stays visible for now — hiding a blocked person's content everywhere has not been built yet.

data.q: Can I get my data out, or delete my account?
data.a: You can download everything you have published as a JSON file from Account settings. Deletion is a request rather than a button: it is reviewed before it completes.

reply.a: There is no honest answer to that yet, so there is no promise. Tickets go into a queue that a person moves through open, in progress and resolved. If you have not heard back, sending the same reference again is fine.

email.q: Who can see my email address?
email.a: Not the public. Email addresses are not shown on profiles and are kept out of the sitemap. A support ticket stores the address you gave it, and only you and platform admins can read that ticket.

guidelines.lastUpdated: Last checked against the app on July 30, 2026
guidelines.title: Community guidelines
guidelines.intro: One set of rules, for every species and every kind of keeper. Each one maps to something the app or a reviewer can actually do — there are no rules here that nobody can enforce.
guidelines.footer: Something unclear, or something the report button does not cover?
guidelines.enforcementBody: Enforcement starts with a report. A person reviews it and can dismiss it, hide the reported content, or suspend the account, and every action taken is recorded against that report.
guidelines.enforcementLimits: In practice that means nothing is scanned automatically and nobody is watching a live feed. Things get looked at because somebody reported them. If you see something wrong, report it — that is the mechanism.

species.title: Every species gets the same standard
species.body: Dogs and cats do not get a better product here than rabbits, birds, reptiles, fish or anything else people keep, and they do not get a worse one either. Nothing on Scrlpets treats an animal as less of an animal because of its species or breed.

honest.title: Describe the animal honestly
honest.body: Species, age, what is known about health and history, and what a buyer or adopter is actually getting. Misrepresenting an animal is grounds for the listing to be hidden and the account suspended.

tooYoung.title: Do not list an animal too young to leave
tooYoung.body: Where a dog's or cat's birth date is recorded and puts the animal under eight weeks old, or where a weaning date is still in the future, the app refuses the listing outright. An unrecorded date is treated as unknown rather than as proof of anything — but offering an underage or unweaned animal breaks this rule whether or not the app can see it.

welfare.title: No cruelty, no unlawful sales
welfare.body: Do not promote cruelty or neglect, and do not use Scrlpets to work around the breeding, sale or transport requirements that apply where you are. Content and accounts can be removed for this.

people.title: Be decent to people
people.body: No harassment, no bullying, no pile-ons, and no impersonating another person or organisation. Disagreeing about how an animal should be kept is fine; going after the person is not.

spam.title: No spam and no scams
spam.body: No fraudulent listings, no scam attempts, and no flooding the app with the same content. If something reads like a scam, report it — that reason is in the report menu.

ownContent.title: Post what is yours
ownContent.body: Photos and video of animals you actually keep or bred, or content you hold the right to publish. You keep ownership of what you post; publishing it gives Scrlpets permission to host and display it so the app can work.

adults.title: Accounts are for adults
adults.body: You must be at least 18 to hold a Scrlpets account, to publish, or to take part in the marketplace. Browsing public content does not require an account.

money.title: Money happens off Scrlpets — be careful
money.body: Scrlpets does not process payments, hold funds, or refund them. If you send money to someone you met here, that is between the two of you and Scrlpets cannot reverse it. Keeping the conversation in Scrlpets messages at least leaves a record of what was agreed.

waitlist.body: A marketplace where how animals are kept matters as much as whether they're available. Leave an email and you'll get one note when it opens.
